summary: Board holds five claims for the GW6 window (closes 9 October) after this morning's sweep, with one real change: Leeds' own team news for today's Palace game has Bogle benched for the first time all season (James Justin in at right wing-back), so claim 2 firms up from low to medium confidence. Elsewhere today's live GW5 round reconfirmed the picture - Marmoush and Van Hecke both pencilled into Tottenham's XI for the Villa game, Haaland/Gvardiol both set to start for City. Sunderland's deadline-day, up-to-GBP30m capture of Malick Fofana from Lyon is a new-arrival blind spot exactly like Barcola's, but he is not a squad player and has yet to start a Premier League match, so it stays a headline rather than a claim. Marcus has now pulled clear of Justin on points (231 to 230), which resolves last night's tie and moves Justin up to 4th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order, better than last night's 5th.

claims.why: Both keepers are undisputed starters with clean bills of health, so this is fixture value rather than fitness - no permitted source raised any doubt over either man's status this week. Hull's run over the next five is simply kinder than Everton's.
claims.model: Model has Tzolakis at 19.1 next5 (avail 1.00) against Pickford's 16.7 (avail 1.00) - a pure fixture gap, not an availability one. This rests on the model's own numbers rather than any news, so no sources are cited beyond that.

claims.why: Reversing last week's reasoning: Leeds' own team news for today's Palace game has Bogle among the substitutes, with James Justin retained at right wing-back and Joe Rodon and Jaka Bijol both restored to the back three. A week ago he was Newcastle's own Hisense Player of the Match after scoring in the 4-1 win, so this reads as rotation rather than a fitness concern, but it is the first time all season a permitted source has actually left him out of the XI. Truffert is a nailed Bournemouth left-back with a kinder run over the same five gameweeks.
claims.model: Model has Truffert at 18.0 next5 (avail 1.00) against Bogle's 14.3 (avail 0.89) - the 0.89 figure has not caught up with today's benching at all, so the real gap is probably larger than the model shows. Upgraded from low to medium confidence on the back of it.

claims.why: Both are fit, nailed starters - Brentford's own preview for Friday's Chelsea game raises no fitness concern over Lewis-Potter, and Leeds' Farke separately reports an almost fully fit squad. Stach was also named this week in Jurgen Klopp's first Germany squad, reported recognition for his form since joining from Hoffenheim. This is a fixture swap, not a news-driven one, and it is deliberately not Barcola: he has started Liverpool's last two games and Alexander Isak this week publicly backed him to make the side 'much better as a team' - the same blind spot the model had on Marmoush and Munoz in August, not a real drop case despite his rock-bottom number.
claims.model: Model has Stach at 18.3 next5 (avail 1.00) against Lewis-Potter's 13.7 (avail 0.95); separately, it rates Barcola at just 3.3 next5, which is why its own greedy board proposes Gross-for-Barcola at +15.1 instead of this swap. Declining it again anyway: nothing this week has surfaced to challenge Barcola's last two starts, so taking the smaller, safer fixture edge here instead.

claims.why: Marmoush remains Tottenham's clear first-choice striker - De Zerbi has started him in every game since his move from City, most recently through Wednesday's Carabao Cup exit - but he is still without a Premier League goal, and said this week the squad is 'working hard' to fix a goalless start. McBurnie is a nailed, in-form Hull striker with a kinder run. This is a speculative, form-only punt against a player whose underlying role is not actually in question, so it is ranked below the fitness- and fixture-driven claims above.
claims.model: Model has McBurnie at 13.1 next5 (avail 0.98) against Marmoush's 9.1 (avail 0.58) - the avail figure looks light for a player who has not missed a minute through injury, so the real gap is probably smaller than +4.0. Kept at low confidence for that reason.

claims.why: Speculative punt on the model's blind spot for new arrivals, the same one that undersold Barcola, Munoz and Schuster for weeks. Crystal Palace's own team news for the Ipswich game has Quinten Timber partnered with captain Adam Wharton in central midfield, not on the bench - a real Premier League starting role for a Netherlands international the model still rates as a fringe squad player. Scott is the safer body to submit last: a fully fit, nailed Bournemouth starter with no news against him at all, so this only matters if the four claims above all land or fail.
claims.model: Model has Timber at just 5.3 next5 (avail 0.37) against Scott's 17.0 (avail 0.99) - essentially no read on Timber off two career games. Overruling the number on the strength of Palace's own team sheet, not the model's math.

claims.model: Model still rates Fernandez-Pardo bottom of the forward pool (next5 3.9, avail 0.27, now off two games rather than one) against Marmoush's 9.4 (avail 0.58) - and Hull's McBurnie (next5 13.9, avail 0.98) would be the model's own pick to replace Marmoush ahead of Fernandez-Pardo on pure numbers. claims.why: Mitchell scored twice as Palace came from behind twice to win 3-2 at Fulham, and has started all three league games. Munoz went the other way in the same window and came on at 59 minutes for Ola Aina on his Forest debut against Tottenham - Neco Williams has played every minute at wing-back and scored 6 and 7 points doing it. Watch one thing: Ben Chilwell has re-signed for Palace and scored the winner at Fulham with his first touch after replacing Mitchell on 73 minutes.
claims.model: Model has Mitchell at next5 16.4 (avail 0.98) against Munoz at 6.4 (avail 0.34), the widest gap on the board, and Palace have the kindest run in the league by its own fixture term (+0.5), starting at home to Ipswich. Agree - but note the model is reading Munoz off 85 minutes played while his Palace exit was negotiated, so if Glasner puts the man he signed as a right wing-back specialist straight into his back three, this one ages badly.

That removes last night's fresh fitness scare, but the underlying case is unchanged: he still has zero Premier League minutes started this season and goes into Saturday against Fulham fighting Gakpo, Isak and Ngumoha for a place. Le Fee has played 79, 89 and 90 minutes, and scored Sunderland's equalising penalty at Brentford.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 17.0 (avail 1.00) against Barcola at 2.4 (avail 0.16), but most of that gap is the model having zero career matches on a marquee arrival - it is a placeholder, not a judgement. Agree regardless of tonight's cramp/injury correction: Barcola's problem is minutes, not fitness, and that hasn't changed.

Overruling the size of the gap, not its direction. Note Elvedi, the man now preferred over Bijol, is himself a new-to-pool signing the model rates at just 6.5 next5 off two games (avail 0.46) - too thin a sample to claim ahead of Bijol, so Maguire's proven full-season 15.5 is the safer target, not Elvedi.
